sections.label: Taxi fare evasion cases
sections.summary: About 150 taxi fare evasion cases occur monthly out of about 700,000 trips, with 65% involving unidentified evaders that are challenging to resolve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: The number of taxi fare evasion cases is about 150 every month, out of about 700,000 taxi trips.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Sixty-five percent of fare evasion cases involved unidentified fare evaders, which are very challenging to resolve.

sections.label: Fare evasion penalties and recovery
sections.summary: LTA recovered fares in about half of referred cases, and from May higher penalties apply, including fines, jail and mandatory restitution to taxi drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) was able to recover fares for about half of all cases referred to it for investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: To further deter fare evasion, we introduced higher penalties for fare evaders in May this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: If found guilty, fare evaders are liable to a fine of up to $1,000 for first-timers, while subsequent offenders may be fined up to $2,000, or jailed up to six months, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: It is also mandatory for offenders to make restitution payment to taxi drivers.

sections.label: Court cases success rate
sections.summary: Where cases go all the way to the Court, the success rate is about 85%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Where it requires us to go all the way to the Court, the success rate is about 85%.
